nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
The scholars have differed over its meaning. Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh said: it is the dawn (al-ṣubḥ). Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Ḥubulī said: it is Jahannam. It has also been said: it is creation; and it has been said: it is a valley in Jahannam. Abū Jaʿfar said:
When disagreement arises, one must return to the language in which the Quran was revealed, and the Arabs say: "It is clearer than the فلق of the morning and its فرق," meaning the daybreak (al-fajr).

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: ما may be a maṣdar (verbal-noun particle), in which case it needs no ʿāʾid (resumptive pronoun); and it may mean الذي (that which), in which case the hāʾ referring back to it is omitted.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: The scholars have discussed the meaning of الغاسق. From the Prophet ﷺ [it is reported] that it is the moon, and we have mentioned that with its isnad. ʿUqayl narrated from al-Zuhrī, who said: «الغاسق إذا وقب» is the sun when it sets. Abū Jaʿfar said: Most of the exegetes hold that الغاسق is the night, and some of them said: the stars. If one returns to the language, one learns from it that one says غسق when it grows dark; so the views agree, because when the sun sets the night enters, the moon is [seen] at night, and the stars hardly appear except at night. So the meaning becomes: "and from the evil of the night when it enters with its darkness and covers everything." One says وقب when it enters; as for Qatāda's statement "وقب: it went away," it is not known [in the language].

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: [النفاثات is the] plural of نفّاثة, and in the broken plural نوافث. It is said that they were sorceresses in the time of the Prophet ﷺ; he commanded seeking refuge from them because they give the impression that they can benefit or harm, and so a person might incur in his religion something by which he sins. As for sorcery itself, it is false (bāṭil).

nahhas-irab:5-5.t:
Ibn Zayd said: they are the Jews. Someone else said: he is Labīd ibn Aʿṣam, and his daughters are the sorceresses.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The most fitting of what has been said about this is the view of Qatāda, who said: it is for everyone who.... ] ... «[Translator's note: the source text is defective/truncated at this point; it is translated as it stands.]»
